headline: Highest risk is CrewAI’s broad filesystem/network defaults interacting with Whisper’s audio-only, non-writing profile; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the lack of a direct bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and parse tool outputs, while Whisper is a non-interactive audio-speech model with no filesystem write or network egress. No direct shared channel is documented, so only an unusual manual file bridge or wrapper could carry injected instructions from Whisper outputs into CrewAI.
conditions: IF an operator copies Whisper transcripts into CrewAI prompts or files, injected text can influence CrewAI.
IF a wrapper feeds Whisper output into CrewAI as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep Whisper outputs in a separate folder from CrewAI inputs.
Require a human review step before any Whisper transcript is used as instructions.
Strip imperative phrases from transcripts before passing them onward.
Use a read-only handoff file for Whisper output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and has broad network egress, but Whisper has no network egress and only handles audio/speech. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so leakage is mainly possible if the operator places sensitive audio or transcripts into CrewAI’s working directory or tool inputs.
conditions: IF sensitive audio files are stored in CrewAI’s working directory, CrewAI may read them.
IF Whisper transcripts are forwarded into CrewAI prompts, sensitive content can appear in CrewAI outputs.
mitigations: Store sensitive audio outside CrewAI’s working directory.
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents.
Redact transcripts before handing them to CrewAI.
Disable unnecessary CrewAI tool integrations.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the host working directory and spawn subprocesses, while Whisper cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable resource documented, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely; the main risk is only if an external orchestrator gives both agents the same directory or artifact path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, CrewAI can overwrite artifacts produced for Whisper.
IF an orchestrator reuses the same filenames for both agents, outputs can collide.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Use unique filenames per agent run.
Make Whisper inputs read-only.
Run CrewAI and Whisper under separate OS accounts.
requires-engineering: add file-locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew and tool integrations can treat upstream artifacts as inputs, while Whisper produces transcription-like outputs that may be mistaken for authoritative text. Even without direct evidence of a specific pipeline, the default pattern supports A→B handoff with no built-in verification, so transcription errors can cascade into downstream actions.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are used as source text for CrewAI tasks, transcription errors can propagate.
IF CrewAI is configured to act on transcript-derived facts without human review, downstream mistakes can occur.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before acting on transcripts.
Require confidence thresholds for transcript-derived facts.
Keep raw audio linked to every transcript.
Use a checklist for any action based on Whisper output.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks in CrewAI workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Whisper is an open-source audio-speech model with no secrets handled and no network egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to operator-managed data placement rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated audio is passed into CrewAI workflows, the operator must ensure the hosting environment meets policy.
IF transcripts containing personal data are stored in CrewAI workspaces, retention policy mismatches can arise.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated audio in CrewAI workspaces.
Document retention for transcripts and audio separately.
Use region-appropriate storage for any sensitive files.
Review API-key handling in CrewAI before deployment.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls.
